Subject: Deployment follow-up — noisy-neighbor risk & SLA options

Hi Sofia / EdgeBank team,

Thanks again for the time earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Recap (from today's call):
- Primary concern: strong isolation guarantees for production model serving (noisy-neighbor risk is a hard requirement).
- Compliance: SOC 2 + audit logs, and EU data residency for a subset of data (you mentioned some cross-border constraints).
- Traffic profile: rough numbers discussed on call, please confirm below.
- Targets: you called out P95 latency target ~150ms and clear SLOs for availability.

How Redwood can help (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, cost-efficient; we offer per-tenant token-rate limiting and soft isolation but shared inferencing pools can have transient noisy-neighbor effects (we mitigate via smart routing + autoscaling).
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for EdgeBank only. Stronger isolation, guaranteed capacity, and SLA-backed latency/uptime. Recommended for regulated financial workloads with strict isolation needs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed network + optional air-gapped package. Maximum control and auditability — longer lead time and ops overhead.

Outstanding items we need from you to size the right recommendation:
1) Confirm sustained RPS and peak RPS (including burst patterns).
2) Clarify whether you require physical isolation (single-tenant GPUs) or whether logical isolation with guaranteed reservations + network isolation is sufficient.
3) Confirm required SLOs (P50/P95/P99 latency, availability %).

Proposed next steps:
- Sofia to share the traffic numbers and SLOs (see items 1–3).
- If Dedicated or Private looks like the fit, we’ll put together a Mutual Action Plan (attached template) and a 30/60/90 timeline.
- Technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Dev) to walk through isolation controls and noisy-neighbor mitigations next week.

I attached a short data sheet on our Dedicated offering and a blank MAP template so you can see timelines. If you’re comfortable, reply with the numbers and your preferred cadence for the technical deep-dive.

Best,
Jonas

Thanks, Jonas — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers below; happy to flesh out in the MAP.

Traffic & SLA:
- Sustained: ~250 RPS of inference requests during business hours (US east).
- Typical payload: 512 tokens average.
- Peaks: up to ~1,100–1,300 RPS during batch job windows (30–45 mins) and occasional ad-hoc spikes up to ~2,000 RPS for short bursts.
- Latency targets: P95 <= 150ms for online inference; P99 as low as possible but we understand tighter P99 is harder.

Isolation requirement:
- Our security team is firm that production inference must not be susceptible to noisy-neighbor degradation. Logical isolation (dedicated reserved pools + strong throttling and KV caching per tenant) is acceptable, but they may push for physical isolation for certain regulated flows. We need to see the technical controls and proof points.

Compliance:
- SOC 2 report required during procurement; also need KMS integration for key management and detailed audit logs of inference requests.

Procurement timing:
- We're aiming to select a vendor by end of Q2. Would like a pricing ballpark for a Dedicated reservation that meets the traffic above, plus an option for a Private (VPC) evaluation.

Can you share an example SLA and whether Redwood offers per-tenant resource guarantees (e.g., pinned GPU capacity or credit-based reservation)?

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
EdgeBank — Head of AI Infrastructure
sofia@edgebank.com

Sofia — thanks for the details, very helpful. Attached is a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and our Dedicated data sheet. High-level answers below, and proposed next steps.

High-level recommendation: Dedicated reservation with VPC peering
- Why: matches your isolation requirement while keeping deployment operationally simple. We provide reserved GPU pools that are logically single-tenant (no co-tenancy on the same GPU instance) and an option to extend to physical single-tenant hardware for regulated flows.
- Noisy-neighbor mitigations we can offer: prioritized scheduling inside the dedicated pool, per-tenant QPS shaping, dedicated KV cache namespaces, and external autoscale headroom with pre-provisioned burst capacity. We also offer a hard-cap enforcement mode so noisy clients cannot evict your cached contexts.

SLA & Guarantees:
- We can commit to a P95 latency SLO of 150ms for the configured model profile when on Dedicated with the agreed reservation and burst buffer. Availability SLA options available (99.9% and 99.95%) tied to reserved capacity contracts.
- Carve-outs: SLOs exclude third-party network outages and scheduled maintenance windows (we'll keep a narrow maintenance SLA).

Compliance & operational items:
- SOC 2: we will provide the latest attestation during due diligence (we've operated with several financial customers).
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (cloud KMS providers) and can document the key lifecycle integration.
- Audit logs: per-request logging available, retention configurable as an add-on.

Next steps / timeline:
1) We’ll attach a draft MAP for your review (attached). Please fill in internal owners and procurement timelines.
2) Marissa will follow up with a Dedicated pricing ballpark and a Private/VPC premium option by EOD today.
3) Dev is available for a technical deep-dive on Tue/Thu next week — propose Tue 10am PT; will cover isolation architecture, autoscale behavior, and sample perf runs for your model profile.

Attachments included: mutual-action-plan-edgebank.xlsx, redwood-dedicated-data-sheet.pdf

If that plan works, I’ll book the technical deep-dive and loop in our solutions engineering runbook.

Best,
Jonas
